the role of appraisal and coping in the experience of stress in carers of persons with MS, and the implications for their psychological health and well-being.

this research has provided evidence that coping is an important factor in determining carers’ well-being.

the coping strategies of positive reappraisal and problem-focused coping were the best predictors of positive outcomes in carers of persons with multiple sclerosis, while the coping strategies of self-blame and denial were the best predictors negative outcomes in carers.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

carer coping strategies, and the care-recipients' life satisfaction are related to both positive outcomes (life-satisfaction, benefits, positive affect) and negative outcomes (anxiety and depression).
the carers of people with MS who have more positive coping strategies and who have more positive perceptions of their care-recipient’s life satisfaction are more likely to have positive outcomes.

carer well-being is not just dependent on the carer’s stress appraisal, coping strategies and the carer-care recipient relationship, but is also influenced by care-recipient characteristics, such as life satisfaction.
the coping strategies used by carers of individuals with MS are related to both positive (e.g., life satisfaction, positive affect) and negative (e.g., anxiety, depression) outcomes.
